goal: Bring the main screen (apps/extension/entrypoints/popup/main-screen) up to feature parity with the reference wallet-main-screen.html for the two pieces MainScreenView.tsx's own doc comment explicitly deferred: the account pill's identity avatar, and the total-portfolio-value chart with range tabs -- consuming historical-pricing's new capability rather than re-deriving it.
outcome: The main screen's account pill shows a generated identicon-style avatar next to the account name/address, produced locally in-process via the @dicebear/core + @dicebear/styles npm packages (weave style, or whichever style matches the reference's seed pattern) seeded from the account's address -- no network call to api.dicebear.com or any other host. Below the balance, the screen shows a USD total-portfolio-value figure, a %-change badge, a period label (e.g. 'Last 7 days'), an SVG line/area chart of value over time sourced from historical-pricing's series + estimateHistoricalPortfolioValue, and range tabs (24H/7D/1M/1Y/ALL) that actually switch the chart's data/period, with the %-change and period label updating to match the selected range. Positive/negative visual treatment is expressed through this project's existing token system (packages/ui/src/tokens/theme.css) -- extended with a new negative/decline token if the existing --color-positive has no counterpart, rather than reintroducing the reference's raw --beam-red/--beam-green literals, since the beam colors are identity-only per this project's own brand rule (design-system-pass's single-warning-red-accent rule) and must not be repurposed as the chart's decline color.

requirements.statement: The avatar is generated locally in-process using @dicebear/core + @dicebear/styles (installed as a new apps/extension dependency) -- never a network fetch to api.dicebear.com or any other third-party host. This is a deliberate deviation from the reference HTML, confirmed with the user, driven by this project's existing no-leaked-identity posture (UnlockScreen.tsx's explicit no-per-wallet-identity-on-unlock rule; TokenGlyph.tsx's existing local-only identicon precedent on this same screen).

The chart consumes historical-pricing's getHistoricalUsdPrices-equivalent series and estimateHistoricalPortfolioValue directly -- this layer does not implement its own historical-balance or historical-price logic, and does not fake or placeholder the series (the exact gap MainScreenView.tsx's original doc comment named as deferred).

Charting implementation (hand-rolled SVG matching the reference's path/gradient approach vs. a charting library) is this layer's own build-time decision, weighed against extension bundle-size constraints -- not fixed by this intent. Whichever is chosen, it must render inside the existing main-screen popup surface without requiring a new build step beyond what pnpm wxt build already does.

Never repurpose --color-beam-red/--color-beam-green (identity-only, single-warning-red-accent rule) as the chart's positive/negative color. Reuse --color-positive for the positive/gain state; add a new semantic negative/decline token to packages/ui/src/tokens/theme.css (following --color-positive's own existing pattern and comment style) if none exists yet, rather than a literal color in component code.

Switching a range tab (24H/7D/1M/1Y/ALL) re-fetches or re-slices the historical series for that range and updates the chart, the %-change badge, and the period label together -- no stale combination of chart data and label is shown.

The account pill in apps/extension/entrypoints/popup/main-screen shows a dicebear-generated SVG avatar seeded from the active wallet's address, rendered without any outbound network request (verifiable by the test mocking/asserting no fetch to a dicebear host).

The main screen renders a USD total value, a %-change badge, a period label, an SVG chart, and 5 range tabs (24H/7D/1M/1Y/ALL); clicking a different range tab changes which tab is marked active and updates the chart/%-change/period label to that range's data.

When historical-pricing's series is unavailable (network failure, both sources down), the screen shows this project's existing NetworkErrorBanner pattern rather than a broken or blank chart -- consistent with how main-screen already handles balance-load failure.

pnpm vitest run main-screen pricing passes; pnpm tsc -p packages/core --noEmit passes; pnpm wxt build succeeds with @dicebear/core + @dicebear/styles bundled as a real dependency (declared in apps/extension/package.json, present in pnpm-lock.yaml).
